approval: NOT APPROVED. These are agent proposals for the owner (RDP-003). None is applied. An obligation amendment takes effect only when the operator writes the record given under 'approvalRecord' into kickoff/rehearsal-007/approvals.causa.json (the file the v4 curation pins), the curation names it in obligationAmendments, and the package is recompiled. Every amendment below keeps the baseline text and only adds to what the bound tests must prove: none weakens, removes or reprioritizes an obligation.

requests.title: Approve compiled package v4 as the frozen requirements for November 7
requests.question: Approve requirements-compiled/v4 (baseline BL-CAUSA-INDY-INIT-62df28a559c0, the verification plan named in freeze-manifest.json) as the frozen package, with or without the amendments ODR-V4-02..06?
options: A: approve v4 as compiled, after deciding ODR-V4-02..07
requests.recommendation: A, after deciding ODR-V4-02..07. K3 (READINESS-ASSESSMENT.md) is an agent-then-owner step: the agent cuts the package, the owner approves it.
requests.rationale: The freeze gate requires every owner approval to exist. An agent cannot approve its own package (RDP-003, AR-003).
requests.impact: Until approved, v4 is published as a CANDIDATE and the tag indy-init-requirements-v4.0.0 is not created.

approvalRecord.how: An approving GitHub review by the owner on the freeze pull request, or a record in kickoff/rehearsal-007/approvals.causa.json: {"decision_id": "ODR-V4-01", "action": "approve-package", "package": "requirements-compiled/v4", "plan_digest": "<verification plan digest from freeze-manifest.json>", "approved_by": "kemiller2002", "date": "<date>"}

requests.title: Extend the copy ban and the provenance scan to Rehearsal 7's repository
requests.problem: PERSIST-026 and PAT-13 name indy-init-rehearsal-001 to indy-init-rehearsal-006. Rehearsal 7 has since produced a complete persistence implementation in indy-init-rehearsal-007. Nothing in the baseline forbids the event build from copying it, and PAT-13 would not detect it.

approvalRecord.criterion: It MUST NOT copy, vendor, translate or adapt application source code, tests or scripts from Causa or any earlier rehearsal repository (indy-init-rehearsal-001 to indy-init-rehearsal-006); the same applies to indy-init-rehearsal-007 and every later rehearsal repository.
approvalRecord.rationale: Rehearsal 7 built a persistence implementation after this list was written; the event must still be built from the requirements (ODR-V4-02).

approvalRecord.criterion: It verifies that no F#, C#, JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML or shell file of more than 20 lines in the candidate is byte-identical, after line-ending normalization, to a file of indy-init-rehearsal-001 to indy-init-rehearsal-006, other than files generated by a published Echelon tool; the same comparison also covers indy-init-rehearsal-007, and it is run by a verifier permitted to check out those repositories, never by the implementing agent.
approvalRecord.rationale: Extends PAT-13 to Rehearsal 7 and records who runs it (Rehearsal 7 KD-009: the implementing agent may not access prior rehearsals).

requests.impact: No new implementation work for the build agent; the independent verifier's PAT-13 run gains one comparison repository.

requests.title: Discard replies to superseded requests (stale refresh, late conflict re-read, reordered answers)
requests.problem: Rehearsal 7's third independent review found that a late read of an older GitHub version overwrote another writer's change during conflict resolution (H1), and that a stale refresh could roll the tab back after a save moved it on (M1). The baseline requires Saved only from a matching read-back (PERSIST-007) but says nothing about replies to loads, refreshes, conflict re-reads or reconciliation reads that arrive after the tab has moved on.

approvalRecord.criterion: The test MUST verify that each legal transition reaches the state PERSIST-031 defines, that every illegal input fails closed with a typed fault, and that Saved is reached only from a read-back confirmation; it also verifies that a reply to a request the tab has superseded (an older load, refresh, conflict re-read or reconciliation read, or any reply whose base head or request identity no longer matches the tab's current one) is discarded without changing the state, the base head or the unsaved changes.
approvalRecord.rationale: Closes the stale-reply defect class found by Rehearsal 7's third review (ODR-V4-03).

requests.impact: One additional property in PAT-12 and one invariant (INV-02); requires each request to carry an identity the machine checks. Small implementation cost, closes a defect class that survived two review rounds in Rehearsal 7.

requests.title: Re-authentication keeps the tab's unsaved work
requests.problem: PERSIST-031 offers Reconnect when the credential was refused, and PERSIST-019 asks for confirmation before disconnecting. In Rehearsal 7 Reconnect discarded all unsaved work after a confirmation (open finding M3). The baseline permits that, which contradicts the data-preservation intent of UI-010-O2 ('what data was preserved, and a safe next step') for an expired token.

approvalRecord.criterion: The action is Retry when a retry can succeed, or Reconnect when the credential was refused; Reconnect accepts a new credential for the same repository within the tab, keeps every investigation and every unsaved change in memory, re-checks the new credential's permissions, and then lets the user save again; unsaved changes are dropped only by an explicit, confirmed discard.
approvalRecord.rationale: An expired or revoked token is a recoverable failure; the user's work must survive it (ODR-V4-04).

requests.impact: Connection state machine gains Reauthenticating (state-machines.json SM-CONNECTION); one PAT-15/PAT-07-style browser case. Moderate cost.

requests.title: A way out of a conflict whose GitHub version is deleted or unverifiable
requests.problem: PERSIST-011 makes a deleted or rewritten investigation a conflict, and PERSIST-012's reapply needs a verifiable GitHub version. In Rehearsal 7 a deleted or unverifiable GitHub version left the conflict with no resolution: the work was kept but could never be saved (open finding M4).

approvalRecord.criterion: The application MUST offer three actions: review the differences, reapply my changes to the GitHub version, and discard my changes and load the GitHub version; when the GitHub version was deleted or fails verification, reapply and load are shown as unavailable with that reason, and the application additionally offers to export the tab's unsaved commands as a file the user saves, without writing anything to GitHub or to browser storage.
approvalRecord.rationale: Every conflict must have a resolution that keeps the user's work without overwriting another writer (ODR-V4-05).

alternatives: Export the unsaved commands (recommended: no write, no overwrite)
Re-create the investigation from the tab's version as a new commit when the GitHub version was deleted (a write; needs its own PERSIST-013 analysis)
requests.impact: One conflict sub-state (SM-CONFLICT Unresolvable) and one PAT-05 case. Small cost.

requests.title: Forged provider replies cannot reach a confirmation
requests.problem: PERSIST-023 forbids adapters, view code and test fixtures from constructing Saved. Rehearsal 7 kept that, yet its save process and reply types were public, so in-process code that fabricated GitHub answers could drive the protocol to a confirmation (open findings H2/M2). The baseline does not say whether a confirmation built from fabricated replies is 'produced by the PERSIST-007 read-back'.

approvalRecord.criterion: A compile-time negative check verifies that application code outside the persistence module cannot construct Saved, and also that it cannot construct a provider reply, a read-back result or a confirmation that the save process accepts: provider answers are decoded from the transport inside the persistence module only.
approvalRecord.rationale: Closes the forged-reply route to a confirmation that Rehearsal 7's reviews 2 and 3 left open (ODR-V4-06).

requests.impact: Moves HTTP result decoding into the persistence module; one more PAT-12 negative project. Small to moderate cost.

requests.title: The single-lead schedule does not fit 420 minutes: approve parallel lanes, or decide scope
requests.problem: execution-plan.json computes the timed plan from the work-item estimates. With one continuous lead agent (Plan B; AR-021 prefers it, finding F-007) the lead's work exceeds 420 minutes; with role lanes (Plan A) the critical path fits. Rehearsal 7, run with one lead agent, left 32 P0 requirements unimplemented and 39 not run or not assessed (evidence/FINAL-REPORT.md). No P0 requirement is removed here.
options: A: approve parallel role lanes (domain, ui, persistence, integration) after the T14 interface freeze, with one integration owner and a fresh reviewer lane (Plan A)
B: keep one lead agent and accept that P0 requirements will be reported NOT_RUN at the deadline
C: reprioritize named P0 requirements through operator approval records (RDP-002/003); the agent proposes no list
requests.recommendation: A. It is the only option that keeps every P0 requirement in scope with an estimated finish inside the window.
requests.impact: Changes agent topology (DEC-016) for the event; adds integration hand-offs that the plan schedules after T14 and T17.
